verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: This mostly repeats F143, which already covers the guide raise to 270–285K and the implied H2 of 160–175K, and the known Shield figure of ~66K (4x). The only new detail is the original Feb guide of 210–225K. The combined oncology-plus-Shield FY26 total of ~690K (+~90%) follows directly from D009 plus F143. Merge into F143 rather than keep it as a separate finding.

verdicts.label: 1B
verdicts.note: Fetched the page and confirmed the 1 Aug 2026 rates: 25B 2x150 lane $3,380 ($3,180 at 8+ lanes) and 10B 2x150 lane $2,000 ($1,710). These look like internal rates; external users pay +30.8% overhead (25B ≈ $4,421). The 25B works out to ~$3.4–3.6/Gb, which sits inside the known core range ($2.63–3.51), so it adds a data point, not a new conclusion. Corrections: (1) The 8+ lane discounts are the core's own volume tier, not Illumina discounts. (2) The page gives no read count for the 'Full Wafer $3,310' line and does not clearly label it as Ultima, so the 3.3–3.9x per-read gap is unverified. Drop it or treat it as a hypothesis.

verdicts.label: 1B
verdicts.note: Confirmed the numbers: 1.5B/5B/10B/25B-300 cost $2,794 / $6,831 / $10,275 / $17,196, which is $6.21 / $4.55 / $3.43 / $2.29 per Gb. Non-NCI users pay exactly 2x. But the 10B→25B step of −33% is a restatement of the known within-X step (−24% to −37% at cores). The 2x non-NCI multiplier is a federal cost-recovery policy and says nothing about Illumina's pricing. Saying a 35B 'follows the same ladder' is speculation. The page is undated. It is used in a derived item below.

verdicts.label: 1B
verdicts.note: Checked the numbers against the 8-K: exome/genome revenue $86.0M→$100.3M (+17%) and volume 23,246→30,785 (+32%), so revenue per test fell from ~$3,700 to ~$3,258 (−12%). Q1 was −5%. The FY guide (volume ≥30%, revenue ≥20%) implies about −8%. However, this is GeneDx's payer reimbursement (blended ARR, outpatient genome collection falling 43%→32%). It is not evidence of Illumina $/Gb discounting, so it does not support 1B. It belongs to the reimbursement-gating point in F188 and the derived item below.

verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: The new piece is the sequential analysis plus management's comment that Q2 was weather catch-up and Q3 will not set a record (from the GuruFocus summary, not checked against a transcript). It supports 1C only in the narrow sense that MRD is not accelerating. MRD still grows ~+45–50% y/y, and MRD tests carry little Gb each except Signatera Genome. Low weight.

verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: Natera's women's health HSD growth and the re-acceleration are largely covered by D010. What is new is management saying the growth comes from share gains. Share gains among Illumina-based NIPT labs (Natera, Labcorp, Myriad, BillionToOne) are roughly neutral for Illumina Gb, so this cuts against 1C only weakly. It actually hints that the market is growing more slowly than Natera's own rate (see the derived NIPT item).

verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: Confirmed in the 8-K: Q2 volume 144K vs 159K (−9%), H1 297K vs 332K (−11%), and prenatal revenue −16% in both periods. FY26 revenue was cut to $770–790M 'due to lower Prenatal Health test volumes and more conservative assumptions regarding average revenue per test.' The −9% is already in the known list; the H1, revenue and guide-cut detail is new. This most likely reflects share loss to Natera and BillionToOne, not market contraction, so it shows NIPT maturity only when netted against the gainers (see the derived item).

verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: Confirmed on the Webull transcript: genomes were 32% of insurance-based outpatient volume in Q2, down from close to 40% in Q1; ~30% or slightly lower is expected in H2; reflex volumes exceeded genomes in July for the first time. Corrections: (1) The 45% figure is the whole exome/genome portfolio in Q1 (from the deck), while 32% and 40% are the insurance outpatient channel only, so don't put them on one series. (2) The '15% in 2025' figure is unverified. (3) Many GeneDx tests are trios, so absolute Gb per test may be higher, but the direction holds.

verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: Confirmed: outpatient genome collection is ~32%, flat q/q and down from 43% in Q2'25, and Q3 is expected roughly flat. The ~70% mature-test goal and the Q4/2027 uplift timing were not seen in the fetched excerpt. The statement that cost is not the constraint is the agent's inference, not management's words.

verdicts.label: 1B
verdicts.note: Confirmed quotes: genome costs 'nearly twice as much to produce than exome… almost entirely higher reagent costs,' expected to come down 'as utilization for genome grows and manufacturers advance their technology'; cost per test flat in H2'26 with 'step improvements in 2027.' Linking this to the 35B is our inference, since the CFO named no vendor or product. Part of the expected saving comes from utilization, not from supplier price. This shows a large customer budgeting for lower reagent cost; it is not proof that Illumina will cut prices.

verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: Confirmed in the Q1 deck: revenue guide $540–555M → $475–490M; volume growth 33–35% → ≥30%; exome/genome revenue growth 33–35% → ≥20%. Most of the cut is price and ARR, since the revenue-growth guide fell ~13–15 pts against ~3–5 pts for volume. The volume cut is modest and volume still grows ≥30%. The Q1 shortfall split ($5.5M ARR / $6.5M Fabric and biopharma) and the 'too aggressive' quote come from snippets and were not verified.

verdicts.label: 1C
verdicts.note: Confirmed in the Q2 8-K: Texas Medicaid exome coverage from 1 May 2026; Medi-Cal genome pricing at 100% of Medicare from 1 Jul 2026; Carelon outpatient genome from 14 Jun 2026 (up to 56M lives); Mississippi Medicaid from 1 Jul 2026; 39 state Medicaid programs. Two things offset it: genome mix is falling (F187) and collection rates are flat at ~32% (F188), so near-term Gb gains from new coverage are slow.

derived.label: 1C
derived.claim: GeneDx's falling genome mix means its sequencing Gb grows much more slowly than its ≥30% test-volume guide; a 5-point portfolio mix drop roughly halves Gb growth.
derived.detail: Illustrative Gb per test is ~100 Gb for a genome and ~10 Gb for an exome (singleton; trios scale both). At the Q1'26 portfolio genome share of 45%, the average is ~50.5 Gb per test. At 40% it is ~46 Gb (−9%), and at 35% it is ~41.5 Gb (−18%). So ≥30% test growth turns into roughly +18% Gb (40% mix) or +7% (35% mix). Management is guiding the insurance-outpatient genome share down from ~40% (Q1) to 32% (Q2) and ~30% (H2'26), with reflex exomes outrunning genomes in July. The largest US clinical exome/genome lab therefore adds far less Illumina volume than its test counts suggest.
derived.source_name: GeneDx Q2'26 call (Webull) and Q1'26 deck (SEC); our calc
derived.quote: hovering at around approximately 30%, maybe slightly lower
derived.why_new: The known list has GeneDx test growth (+32%) but no Gb-per-test or mix-adjusted Gb estimate for GeneDx.

derived.label: 1C
derived.claim: Netting Natera's NIPT-heavy gains against Myriad's prenatal losses, combined volume at the two labs grew only ~+8% y/y in Q2'26, so most of Natera's women's health growth is share shift.
derived.detail: Natera non-oncology tests were 747.2K in Q2'26 vs 664.3K (+82.9K). Myriad Prenatal Health was 144K vs 159K (−15K). Combined that is 891.2K vs 823.3K, or +8.2%, against Natera's own +12.5%. For H1, Myriad was 297K vs 332K (−35K). Both labs run on Illumina, so the share shift between them is roughly neutral for Illumina NIPT Gb, and the underlying pool is growing at a high-single-digit rate. Caveats: Natera's non-oncology line includes organ health, Myriad's prenatal line includes carrier screening, and Labcorp and BillionToOne are not netted.
derived.source_name: Myriad Q2'26 8-K Ex. 99.1; Natera Q2'26 release; our calc
derived.why_new: The known list has Myriad −9% and Natera non-oncology separately, but no combined net NIPT-pool growth rate.

derived.label: 1B
derived.claim: GeneDx's statement that a genome costs ~2x an exome, almost all reagents, implies an incremental reagent cost of roughly $2.4–9 per extra Gb, well above negotiated 25B levels (~$1.6–2.3/Gb). This gives it a strong motive to seek supplier price cuts in 2027.
derived.detail: With the known blended cost per test of ~$1,176 and a ~45% genome mix, the cost split is 0.55C + 0.45×2C = 1.45C. That gives an exome cost C of ~$810 and a genome cost of ~$1,620. The ~$810 difference buys ~90–115 extra Gb per singleton (~$7–9/Gb) or ~270–345 Gb per trio (~$2.4–3.0/Gb). Even the trio case sits above the ~$1.6–2.3/Gb negotiated or GSA 25B estimates. The difference probably includes genome library prep, so Illumina's sequencing share of the gap is smaller. The CFO is budgeting 'step improvements in 2027' as manufacturers advance their technology. Heavy assumptions apply: the mix and cost periods differ, and the trio share is unknown.
derived.source_name: GeneDx Q2'26 call (Webull); known GeneDx cost/test; our calc
derived.why_new: No known item converts GeneDx's genome-vs-exome cost gap into an implied reagent $/Gb.

derived.label: 2A
derived.claim: NCI Frederick's internal recharge for a 25B-300 flow cell ($17,196) is ~4% above Illumina's $16,480 list, so this large federal research user does not appear to pass through deep discounts.
derived.detail: NCI Frederick's undated rate page lists the 25B-300 at $17,196 per flow cell for NCI users (non-NCI users pay 2x, $34,392). Against the $16,480 list price (F146), that is +4.3%. Unless overhead and labor are large, the implied reagent cost is near list. This fits the sole-source, uncompeted NIH reagent IDC (F040; $90M ceiling over 5 years). Both cut against the 'insane discounts' picture for government research accounts, though Broad-type large academic centers may differ. Caveat: the recharge rate includes labor and QC, so the actual reagent discount cannot be backed out.
derived.source_name: NCI Frederick Sequencing Facility pricing; F146 list price
derived.why_new: No known item compares a federal facility's flow-cell recharge with Illumina list price.

derived.label: 1C
derived.claim: At GeneDx, revenue per exome/genome test fell ~12% y/y in Q2'26, and the FY26 guide implies ~−8%. Payer economics, not sequencing capacity, gate the lab's growth.
derived.detail: Exome/genome revenue was $100.3M on 30,785 tests in Q2'26, or ~$3,258 per test, vs $86.0M on 23,246 (~$3,700) in Q2'25: −12%. Q1'26 was ~$3,296 vs ~$3,472, or −5%. The FY26 guide of volume ≥30% and revenue ≥20% implies at least −8% per test. Outpatient genome collection fell from 43% to 32% over the same period, and management cut the revenue guide by ~$65M while trimming volume only 3–5 points. A key Illumina clinical customer is therefore limited by reimbursement, which caps how fast it can expand genome (high-Gb) volume.
derived.source_name: GeneDx Q2'26 and Q1'26 8-K/deck; our calc
derived.why_new: The known list has GeneDx volume (+32%) and cost per test, but not its revenue per test or the guide-implied ARPT decline.
